---
title: "Borrowing: Shared `&T` vs Exclusive `&mut T`"
description: "One key Rust idea, one tiny executable example, the reason it works, and a precise pitfall."
---

## The question

**How can a function read a String without taking it away from its caller?**

Borrow using a reference. Many active shared references can read a value; an exclusive mutable reference can modify it when no overlapping incompatible references are being used.

## The core rule

Shared reads may overlap; an exclusive writer must not overlap with those reads.

## One complete example

Paste these lines into `main.rs` and run with `rustc --edition 2024 main.rs && ./main`, or [use the tested Rust examples project](examples/index.qmd).

~~~rust
fn main() {
    let mut name = String::from("Ada");
    let view = &name;
    println!("{view}");         // shared borrow ends at last use
    let edit = &mut name;
    edit.push('!');
    println!("{name}");         // Ada!
}
~~~

**Walk through it:** `view` borrows the String without owning it. After its last use, the borrow checker permits the later mutable borrow `edit`. This is **non-lexical lifetime** behaviour: a borrow need not remain live until the closing brace.

## Mathematical model — explained with real values

$$
W(v)=1\ \Longrightarrow\ R(v)=0
$$

**What every symbol means:** `W(v)` means the number of active exclusive mutable borrows of the value v; `R(v)` is the number of conflicting active shared borrows. This is an instructional abstraction for the borrow rule, not Rust's complete aliasing model.

**Substitute actual values:** While `view` is being used, there is one shared borrow (`R=1`) and no mutable borrow (`W=0`). During the later `edit.push('!')`, there is one active mutable borrow (`W=1`) and no overlapping shared borrow (`R=0`).

## Common misunderstanding

Incorrect: take `let edit = &mut name;` and then still use an earlier `view` later. Rust rejects the conflicting overlap at compile time, rather than racing at runtime.

## Remember it in one sentence

Shared reads may overlap; an exclusive writer must not overlap with those reads.

**Official reference:** [The Rust Programming Language / Rust Reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-02-references-and-borrowing.html).
